descriptionChirho: To be of greater value or worth than something else, used in Jesus' arguments from lesser to greater: humans are worth more than sparrows (Matt 6:26, 10:31, Luke 12:7, 12:24) and a man more than a sheep (Matt 12:12). All these passages use Arb afdal (better/superior), Heb chashuvim/shonim (important/different), Kor gwihanya (precious), Spa valeis-mas (you are worth more), Fra etre-superieur. The Rom 2:18 and Phil 1:10 uses of ta diapheronta (the things that differ/excel) also belong here, referring to discerning what is morally superior or excellent, with Hin uttam (excellent) confirming the evaluative sense.

To be distinct or different from something else, marking qualitative difference without necessarily implying superiority. Found in 1 Cor 15:41 where one star differs from another in glory and Gal 4:1 where an heir in his minority differs nothing from a slave. Cross-linguistic glosses uniformly reflect distinction rather than value: Heb shoneh (different), Kor dareunira/dareuji-anhnora (differs/does not differ), Spa difiere (differs), Deu sich-unterscheiden (distinguish oneself), Arb yakhtalif (differs). This is genuinely distinct from the evaluative 'surpass' sense.

To be of importance or make a difference in a given situation, an impersonal use meaning 'it matters.' Occurs in Gal 2:6 where Paul says the reputed pillars' status makes no difference to him (ou diapherein). Arb yufriq (makes a difference), Heb meshanneh (changes/matters), Kor dareuji-anheuni (does not differ), Spa importa (matters). While related to the 'differ' sense, the impersonal construction with evaluative force (it matters/it makes no difference) warrants separate treatment as a distinct pragmatic usage.

Physical carrying or being borne along, the original concrete sense of dia+phero. Mark 11:16 prohibits carrying vessels through the temple (Arb yahmil, Heb ya'avir, Kor unbanhadorok, Spa llevara). Acts 13:49 describes the word of the Lord being carried/spread through the region (Arb intasharat, Heb nissa, Kor pyeojyeotda, Spa era-difundida). Acts 27:27 uses the passive of sailors being driven about in the Adriatic (Arb munjariafeen, Heb nischafim, Kor tteodoneun, Spa siendo-llevados). All three share the physical transfer or conveyance meaning, clearly distinct from the abstract evaluative senses.
